question: A project's instructions say "always write in plain language for non-specialists" and, further down, "use the full technical terminology our engineers expect". Team members report that outputs vary widely. What is the greatest concern with these instructions as written?
options: A) Claude will merge the two rules into one style that always sits exactly halfway between the two audiences.
B) Instructions longer than a few lines are ignored, so only the very first rule in the list will ever be applied.
C) The two rules conflict, so Claude has no reliable basis for choosing a register and results vary between chats.
D) Conflicting rules cause the project knowledge base to be reindexed, which slows down every answer given.
correct_answers: C) The two rules conflict, so Claude has no reliable basis for choosing a register and results vary between chats.
explanations: A predictable midpoint is not what happens; the observed symptom is inconsistency, not a stable compromise.
There is no such rule that only the opening line of project instructions is read.
Correct. Contradictory house rules are the direct cause: neither rule can be satisfied without breaking the other.
Instruction wording does not trigger any reprocessing of uploaded documents.
